key_insight: A plane-wave, GPU-accelerated BSE force formulation enables practical analytical excited-state relaxation calculations for large solid-state systems without empty-state summations or per-displacement response runs.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable route to predict defect relaxation and vibronic effects in heterogeneous materials at near first-principles excited-state accuracy.
method: Combine density-matrix perturbation theory with a Lagrangian formulation for analytical nuclear forces.
Avoid explicit empty-state summations and repeated DFPT-style displacement responses.
Use GPU acceleration to make BSE forces tractable for systems with hundreds of atoms.
evidence_signal: The method is demonstrated on two defects—NV center in diamond and a carbon-dimer defect in hBN—showing agreement with TDDFT in one case and a BSE-corrected relaxation pattern in the other.
watch_item: The approach is computationally advanced and implementation-heavy, so performance and robustness may depend on efficient GPU support and accurate screening for diverse heterogeneous systems.
paper_title: Analytical Forces from the Bethe-Salpeter Equation for Large-Scale Excited-State Relaxation
